findings.message: Only the homepage forwards GitHub's `error=redirect_uri_mismatch&state=…` return to the callback. When the Redirect URI was saved incorrectly, GitHub sends the person back to whatever URI is registered, and that may not be the homepage. Paths that will happen include `/git-accounts` (this module's own page), `/signin` and Auth.js's `/api/auth/callback/github`. None of these forward the return, so the claim is never recorded as `callback` and nobody is told what to fix. Fix the whole class: forward this return wherever it lands (for example in the app layout or middleware, or on any (app) route with `state` plus `error=redirect_uri_mismatch`), or have Git accounts treat a connect state left unresolved past its expiry as a likely callback problem. The test (app-116 'final pass') calls `githubCallback` directly. It never drives the page's forward, so deleting this line leaves every test green. Add a test that drives the real request path over at least three landing paths.
findings.scenario: An Admin registers https://amax.example/git-accounts as the Redirect URI. Kasun confirms Connect GitHub, and GitHub redirects to /git-accounts?error=redirect_uri_mismatch&state=…. The Git accounts page renders as normal and the connect state never becomes 'callback'. Settings never shows the fix.

findings.message: Only `redirect_uri_mismatch` at the token exchange is turned into a refusal that says what to fix. The other configuration errors GitHub returns there, such as `incorrect_client_credentials` (a wrong Client secret), fall through to `GitHubReplyError`. That error says 'GitHub didn't answer or its reply wasn't readable. Try again'. Retrying can never succeed: an Admin has to replace the app. The secret check (20+ characters, no whitespace or `:`) accepts a mistyped secret, so this path is easy to reach. Map `incorrect_client_credentials` (and similar errors that mean the app is misconfigured) to a result that tells an Admin to set the app up again. Add table-driven cases for these errors.
findings.scenario: An Admin pastes a 40-character secret from another GitHub app. Every person's connect then fails at the token exchange with `{error:'incorrect_client_credentials'}`, and each person is told 'GitHub didn't answer… Try again' forever.

findings.message: The server page calls get_github_app_status through the registry with `source: "chat"`. This is a UI read, so any trace or permission logic that depends on the source will mislabel it. Use the UI source, as other settings pages do with `contextForViewer(viewer, "ui")`.
findings.scenario: An Admin opens Settings › Integrations. The read is recorded or treated as a chat call.

findings.message: `until` starts as `{}` and is filled in by an effect. As a result, a snoozed nudge appears on first paint and then disappears. Either hide nudges until the stored value has been read, or accept the flicker and document it.
findings.scenario: Kasun clicks 'Not now' and reloads Overview. 'Connect GitHub' shows briefly, then vanishes.

findings.message: When the table holds only nudges, the 'Select all decisions' checkbox is still shown and does nothing. Hide or disable it when `decisions` is empty.
findings.scenario: Kasun has only the Connect GitHub nudge. Checking 'Select all decisions' selects nothing.

findings.message: This git-accounts change also edits platform code (packages/core/src/secrets/expiry.ts, packages/core/src/module.ts, packages/core/src/overview.ts, packages/ai/src/scripted.ts and apps/web). It declares no lane exemption, unlike 108's 'Lane exemption:' line. Add the exemption naming those platform pieces.

`configured` only checks that a github-oauth credential exists (`hasSecret`). It never checks that the stored value is a usable `<client id>:<client secret>`. This change builds three new paths on that flag: the Overview nudge (`overview.ts`), the Admin suggestions (Rotate or Remove, never Set up), and the Integrations chip "Configured". Meanwhile `app()` is now stricter: it refuses any value that splits into more than two parts. A value that `app()` refuses is therefore reported as configured. Fix: have the status classify the stored value with the same parse `app()` uses, one shared function and not a second copy. Report it as `incomplete` (not configured). The nudge then stays hidden, and the suggestions and chip offer Set up the GitHub app.
findings.scenario: A tenant stored github-oauth through 108's put_secret as `only-the-secret-…` (or `id:sec:ret`, which the old first-colon split accepted). After 116: Integrations shows "Configured", Admins are offered only "Rotate the GitHub app secret", and every person is nudged on Overview to Connect GitHub. Every connect then fails with APP_INCOMPLETE.

findings.message: The credential format still has two definitions that disagree. The write side (`checkClientId`: 4–100 characters with no whitespace, `<`, `>` or `:`; `checkClientSecret`: at least 20 characters with no whitespace or `:`) is stricter than the read side in `app()`, which accepts any two non-empty parts. Put one `parseGitHubApp(value)` next to the checks and use it in both `app()` and the status.
findings.scenario: A stored value `ab:x` is accepted by `app()` and sent to GitHub, although `set_github_app` would refuse both parts.
